_note: Run: <torch-venv>/bin/python bin/mutate.py --spec mutations/ijepa-backbone.json --python <torch-venv>/bin/python (an interpreter with torch, so the backbone builds and loads in-process). This is the A3:ijepa wiring (docs/STEP3_PORTING_PLAN.md): I-JEPA reused as a frozen spatial-backbone kind for the ARSSL harness. The MAE-specific provider lives in the method's own directory (methods/29_ijepa/downstream_backbone.py) and the shared layer (downstream/spatial_backbones.py) DISCOVERS it, naming no method -- so no shared-layer edit was needed and the shared discovery/dispatch/KINDS guards are already proven in mutations/mae-backbone.json. These guards prove the I-JEPA provider itself is not vacuous: a checkpoint that is not this encoder is refused (both directions: alien keys and missing weights) and the backbone stays frozen in eval. I-JEPA has no CLS token (no prefix to drop) and no decoder (a plain, exact match), so it carries fewer provider-side guards than MAE by design.

targets.label: an encoder carrying keys this I-JEPA does not have is half-loaded, not refused
an encoder missing the backbone weights is silently accepted
the backbone leaves eval when train() is called
